title: Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of bracket, open brackets are closed in the correct order, and every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.

title: Two Sum
statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
You can return the answer in any order.

title: Merge Sorted Array
statement: You are given two nondecreasing integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, plus counts m and n for their initialized portions.
nums1 has length m + n, with its final n slots reserved as empty space. Merge nums2 into nums1 so nums1 becomes one sorted array in place.

title: Remove Element
statement: Given an integer array nums and a value val, remove every occurrence of val in place.
Return the number of remaining elements. The first returned-length items of nums must contain exactly those remaining elements; their order does not matter.

examples.output: 5, nums starts with [0,1,3,0,4] in any order

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement: Given a nondecreasing integer array nums, compact it in place so each distinct value appears once.
Return the number of distinct values. The first returned-length items of nums must hold those values in their original sorted order.
constraints: nums is sorted in nondecreasing order.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
statement: Given a nondecreasing integer array nums, compact it in place so each distinct value appears at most twice.
Return the length of the kept prefix. The first returned-length items must preserve the original sorted order.
constraints: nums is sorted in nondecreasing order.

title: Majority Element
statement: Given an integer array nums, return the value that appears more than half of the time.
The input always contains such a majority value.

title: Rotate Array
statement: Given an integer array nums, rotate it to the right by k steps in place.
After rotation, each element moves k positions to the right, wrapping around to the front as needed.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement: Given daily stock prices, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell.
Return the largest possible profit. If no profitable sale exists, return 0.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
statement: Given daily stock prices, return the largest profit you can make with as many buy-sell transactions as you want.
You may hold at most one share at a time, so each sell must happen before the next buy.

title: Jump Game
statement: Given an array nums where nums[i] is the farthest jump length from index i, decide whether you can reach the last index from index 0.
You may choose any jump length from 0 up to nums[i] at each position.

title: Jump Game II
statement: Given an array nums where nums[i] is the farthest jump length from index i, return the fewest jumps needed to reach the last index.
The input always allows reaching the last index.

title: H-Index
statement: Given an array citations where citations[i] is the citation count for one paper, return the researcher's h-index.
The h-index is the largest h such that at least h papers have h or more citations.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
statement: Design a set of integers that supports insert, remove, and getRandom.

insert(val) adds val if absent and reports whether it was added. remove(val) deletes val if present and reports whether it was removed. getRandom() returns one current value, with each stored value equally likely.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^5 calls will be made.
getRandom is called only when the set is non-empty.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every nums[j] except nums[i].
Do this without using division.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Gas Station
statement: There are gas stations arranged in a circle. gas[i] is the fuel gained at station i, and cost[i] is the fuel needed to drive from station i to the next station.
Return the index of a station from which you can complete the full circuit, or -1 if no such start exists.

title: Candy
statement: Given ratings for children standing in a line, give each child at least one candy.
Any child with a higher rating than an immediate neighbor must receive more candies than that neighbor. Return the minimum total candies needed.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Given nonnegative bar heights, compute how much rain water is trapped after raining.
Water above a position is limited by the shorter of the tallest bar to its left and the tallest bar to its right.

title: Roman to Integer
statement: Given a valid Roman numeral, convert it to its integer value.
Roman symbols normally add from left to right, but a smaller symbol before a larger one subtracts instead.
constraints: s contains only I, V, X, L, C, D, and M.
s is a valid Roman numeral in the range 1 to 3999.

title: Integer to Roman
statement: Given an integer, convert it to a Roman numeral.
Use the standard subtractive forms such as IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, and CM when they apply.

title: Length of Last Word
statement: Given a string containing words separated by spaces, return the length of the final word.
A word is a maximal group of non-space characters, and the string may contain leading or trailing spaces.

examples.input: s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "

constraints: s consists of English letters and spaces.
There is at least one word in s.

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement: Given an array of strings, return the longest prefix shared by every string.
If no non-empty prefix is common to all strings, return the empty string.
constraints: strs[i] contains only lowercase English letters when non-empty.

title: Reverse Words in a String
statement: Given a string, return the words in reverse order separated by a single space.
Trim leading and trailing spaces, and collapse multiple spaces between words in the result.
constraints: s contains English letters, digits, and spaces.
There is at least one word in s.

title: Zigzag Conversion
statement: Write the characters of a string across a zigzag pattern with the given number of rows, then read the rows from top to bottom.
Return the resulting string without drawing the grid explicitly.
constraints: s consists of English letters, comma, and period.

title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
statement: Given two strings, return the first index where needle appears in haystack.
Return -1 if needle is not present.
constraints: haystack and needle consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Text Justification
statement: Given a list of words and a maximum line width, format the words into fully justified text.
Each line must have exactly maxWidth characters. Non-final lines spread spaces as evenly as possible, with extra spaces assigned to earlier gaps. The final line is left-justified.
constraints: words[i] contains only English letters and symbols.

title: Valid Palindrome
statement: Given a string, determine whether it reads the same forward and backward after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and letter case.
Digits and letters both count as comparable characters.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters.

title: Is Subsequence
statement: Given strings s and t, return whether s is a subsequence of t.
A subsequence keeps relative order but may delete characters from t.
constraints: s and t consist only of lowercase English letters.

title: Container With Most Water
statement: Given vertical line heights, choose two lines that form a container holding the most water.
The area is the distance between the two lines multiplied by the shorter height.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers, return the two indices whose values add to target.
Exactly one answer exists, and the first returned index must be smaller than the second.
constraints: numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: 3Sum
statement: Given an integer array, return all unique triplets whose values sum to zero.
The output must not contain duplicate triplets.

title: Happy Number
statement: Repeatedly replace a positive integer with the sum of the squares of its digits.
Return true if the process reaches 1, and false if it enters a cycle that never reaches 1.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Given a string, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.
A substring must be contiguous.
constraints: s consists of letters, digits, symbols, and spaces.

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Given strings s and t, return the shortest substring of s containing every character from t with the required multiplicity.
Return the empty string if no such window exists.
constraints: s and t consist of English letters.
The answer is unique when it exists.

title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
statement: Given a string and a list of equal-length words, return every starting index where a substring is formed by concatenating each word exactly once.
The words may be used in any order, but every listed word and its multiplicity must be used.
constraints: s and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement: Given a target and an array of positive integers, return the smallest length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target.
Return 0 if no such subarray exists.

title: Valid Sudoku
statement: Given a 9 x 9 Sudoku board, determine whether the filled cells obey Sudoku rules.
Each row, each column, and each 3 x 3 box may contain digits 1 through 9 at most once. Empty cells are marked with '.'.
constraints: board[i][j] is a digit '1' through '9' or '.'.

title: Spiral Matrix
statement: Given an m x n matrix, return every value in clockwise spiral order.
Start at the top-left corner, walk across the top row, then continue around the remaining boundary until all cells are visited.

title: Rotate Image
statement: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in place.
Modify the input matrix directly; do not return a separate rotated matrix.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix, if any cell is 0, set its entire row and column to 0.
Modify the matrix in place, and base all changes on the zeroes present before the update starts.

title: Game of Life
statement: Given a board of live cells (1) and dead cells (0), compute the next state of Conway's Game of Life.
Every cell updates simultaneously from the original board using its eight neighbors, and the board must be modified in place.

title: Ransom Note
statement: Given two strings, ransomNote and magazine, return whether ransomNote can be built using letters from magazine.
Each character from magazine may be used at most once.
constraints: ransomNote and magazine consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Isomorphic Strings
statement: Given two strings s and t, return whether s can be transformed into t by replacing each character consistently.
Each character in s must always map to the same character in t, and no two different characters in s may map to the same character in t.
constraints: s and t consist of ASCII characters.

title: Word Pattern
statement: Given a pattern and a space-separated string s, return whether s follows the same pattern.
There must be a one-to-one mapping between each pattern character and each word in s.
constraints: s contains lowercase English letters and spaces, with words separated by a single space.

title: Valid Anagram
statement: Given two strings s and t, return whether t is an anagram of s.
An anagram uses exactly the same characters with exactly the same counts, in any order.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Group Anagrams
statement: Given an array of strings, group together strings that are anagrams of each other.
The groups and the strings inside each group may be returned in any order.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Contains Duplicate II
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return whether two equal values appear at indices whose distance is at most k.
The pair must use different indices.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values.
The values in the run do not need to appear next to each other in the array.

title: Summary Ranges
statement: Given a sorted unique integer array, summarize every maximal consecutive run.
A single number is written as itself, and a run of at least two numbers is written as start->end.
constraints: nums is sorted in strictly increasing order.

title: Insert Interval
statement: Given sorted non-overlapping intervals and one new interval, insert the new interval and merge overlaps.
Return sorted non-overlapping intervals covering the original intervals plus the new one.
constraints: intervals is sorted by start and has no overlaps.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
statement: Each balloon is an interval on the x-axis. One arrow shot at x bursts every balloon whose interval contains x.
Return the minimum number of arrows needed to burst all balloons.

title: Simplify Path
statement: Given an absolute Unix-style path, return its simplified canonical path.
Single dots do nothing, double dots move up one directory when possible, and repeated slashes behave like one slash.
constraints: path is an absolute path beginning with '/'.
path contains English letters, digits, '.', '/', and '_'.

title: Min Stack
statement: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the current minimum value.
Each operation must run in O(1) time.
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getMin are called only when the stack is non-empty.
At most 3 * 10^4 calls will be made.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement: Given tokens for a valid arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation, evaluate the expression.
Operators are +, -, *, and /. Division between integers truncates toward zero.
constraints: tokens[i] is an operator or an integer in range [-200, 200].
The input is a valid Reverse Polish Notation expression.
All intermediate and final results fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

title: Basic Calculator
statement: Given a valid arithmetic expression string s, evaluate it and return its integer value.
The expression may contain nonnegative integers, '+', '-', parentheses, and spaces.
constraints: s consists of digits, '+', '-', '(', ')', and spaces.
Every number and final answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
